headline: On November 25, 1975: Suriname gains independence from the Netherlands
captionCards: 95% of Suriname's land is covered by rainforest
Suriname remains the smallest sovereign country in South America by both population and territory
instagramCaption:
Suriname becomes independent on November 25, 1975.


The Republic of Suriname officially separates from the Netherlands after years of colonial rule.
It is located on the northern coast of South America, bordered by Guyana, Brazil, and French Guiana.
Over 95% of its territory is covered by rainforest—the second-highest forest cover proportion in the world.
Paramaribo, the capital, houses roughly half the population of about 612,985 people.

This moment marks the start of Suriname’s sovereignty as a nation with unique cultural and environmental identity.
